newsitem.title: USA: Antofagasta to gain Forestal stake.
newsitem.headline: Antofagasta to gain Forestal stake.

text.p: Chile's Forestal Quinenco SA said on Thursday that it has tentatively agreed to merge two Antofagasta Holdings Plc subsidiaries with Quinenco for 39.25 percent of Quinenco's common stock.
Quinenco is merging with Antofagasta's Andes Trust Ltd and Anaconde Chile, forming a company with pro-forma revenues of US$1.4 billion for 1995, the company said.
Antofagasta and Quinenco are both controlled by Andronico Luksic Sr, Quinenco said.

Quinenco is a diversified Chilean company with interests that include 28.6 percent of Madeco SA, 33.3 percent of beverage firm Compania Cervercerias Unidas SA, 12 percent of telecommunications firm VTR SA, 75.7 percent of Lucchetti SA, Hoteles Carrera and various banking interests.
The holdings of Andes Trust Ltd and Anaconda Chile include 24.9 percent of Madeco, 14.5 percent of VTR and various interests in the banks described above.
After the merger, Quinenco said it will acquire an additional 14.5 percent stake in VTR. It will then hold controlling interests in Madeco, VTR, Lucchetti and Hoteles Carrera, Quinenco said.
Quinenco also said it is in the process of completing its partnership with Banco Central Hispanoamericano of Spain to form a financial services group for South America.

This group will control interests in Banco O'Higgins and Banco de Santiago in Chile, Argentina's Banco Tornquist, Paraguay's Banco de Asuncion SA, Centro Hispano Banco SA in Uruguay and Banco del Sur in Peru.

Shareholders' meetings have been called for September 30, 1996 and if approved at such meetings, the merger is expected to become effective on that date. Morgan Stanley is advising Quinenco in connection with these transactions.
